analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/startup-shape-warmup.md, lines 1-3) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 442-448). No source code is supplied, so the warmup implementation (ProviderLoop preload, IdleCalibrationCoordinator, MLX pool sweep) is unreviewed.

Security-relevant claims in the docs: (1) the warmup runs after model load and any self-test, before provider registration and before the local listener opens. This leaves the TB-002/TB-011 registration, attestation and authorization paths unchanged. It does add up to 20 s per model of startup latency, a bounded availability effect (T-057-adjacent), and the stated 'within 20 seconds' limit is enforced in code that was not supplied. (2) The warmup uses the existing calibration session, idle gate and foreground lease. It runs within the existing KV and service budgets and publishes no observations or work totals. This is consistent with the existing text at lines 411-415 that calibration does not raise concurrency or lower reserves. (3) Warmup cells use synthetic prompts. Whether they interact with the SSD prefix cache (T-041) is not stated: a donation of synthetic data or a TTFT-oracle effect would need checking in code. The docs say warmup publishes no observations, but not whether it bypasses prefix-cache donation. (4) The proactive MLX pool sweep waits while a session runs, while on-pressure reclaims still run. This is a minor memory-pressure/T-028 residual-GPU-memory consideration, and the wait is bounded by session length.

`DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP` is a local env knob that only disables or forces the warmup. It is not an attacker-controlled input across a trust boundary. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the documentation. Remaining questions for the code PR: that prompts are synthetic and contain no consumer data, that the prefix-cache donation path is skipped, and that the 20 s timeout and cancellation work.
